name_review_base.evidence: Genesis 9 closes the account of Noah, the flood survivor and son of Lamech, by recording his death at 950.

analysis.evidence: כָּל יְמֵי נֹחַ means “all the days of Noah,” and the numerical predicate gives their total as nine hundred and fifty years. וַיִּהְיוּ links Noah’s lifespan to that total.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural, with prefixed וַ־. The verb agrees with the masculine plural יְמֵי in כָּל יְמֵי נֹחַ.
analysis.sense: to be (of a quantity or duration), to amount to

analysis.evidence: The verse gives one total of 950 years for כָּל יְמֵי נֹחַ, “all the days of Noah.” Thus כָּל takes Noah’s days together as his entire lifespan.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun governing יְמֵי נֹחַ, “the days of Noah.”

analysis.evidence: כָּל יְמֵי נֹחַ means “all the days of Noah.” The verse gives their total as 950 years and then records his death, so the phrase refers to his whole lifetime.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural construct of the common noun יוֹם, with נֹחַ (Noah) as its complement.
analysis.sense: (pl.) days of a life, a reign or an age

analysis.evidence: כָּל יְמֵי נֹחַ means “all the days of Noah.” The verse totals his lifespan at 950 years and closes with וַיָּמֹת, “and he died.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name without a prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase יְמֵי נֹחַ, “the days of Noah.”

analysis.evidence: תְּשַׁע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה means ‘nine hundred years’. The following וַחֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה adds fifty years, giving Noah a lifespan of 950 years.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular cardinal numeral, parsed as absolute, with no prefix or suffix. It counts the feminine plural מֵאוֹת ‘hundreds’.
analysis.sense: Nine as the multiplier in ‘nine hundred’.

analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, feminine plural absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)
